- AWS account (primary): 111122223333 (us-east-1)

- Primary security contact: samir.kaur@curetech.com
- Procurement contact: procurement@curetech.com

Can you send the staging/onboarding checklist and the network egress/ingress matrix we need to open on our side? Also please confirm: do you require a customer-managed NAT, or do you recommend Redwood-managed egress via PrivateLink?

Thanks,
Nicola Baines
VP Product Operations | CureTech Labs

Subject: Re: Private deployment — target July 30th, initial info

Nicola —

Appreciate the details. We can support the July 30th target with a 3-phase staged onboarding: discovery -> connectivity sprint -> validation & go/no-go. Attached is our recommended staging checklist (redwood-staged-onboard-checklist-v1.xlsx) and a compact egress/port matrix. High-level notes below and explicit ownership so we don't miss anything.

Staged onboarding summary (short):
1) Discovery (this week) — owners: CureTech (network) + Redwood SE (laura_bennett)
   - Confirm account IDs, VPC/subnet CIDRs, routing model (peering vs. TGW), and AWS Org settings.
   - Share NTP/DNS, proxy, and outbound inspection ownership.

2) Connectivity sprint (7 calendar days) — owners: CureTech network + Redwood infra (alex_martinez)
   - Establish secure egress (we recommend AWS PrivateLink for control; we can support customer NAT if required).
   - Open minimal ports, deploy test endpoint in your VPC, configure mutual TLS (mTLS) with our edge.
   - Validate route propagation, MTU sizes for GPU model payloads, and BGP health if using TGW.

3) Validation & smoke (2 days) — owners: CureTech app + Redwood QA (marissa_cole)
   - Smoke tests: tokenized throughput, 95th pct latency under 4KB prompts, KV cache persistence test, continuity across minor rolling restarts.
   - Security checks: KMS key access, audit-log ingestion, and intrusion detection alerts firing to your SIEM.

Acceptance criteria (must be green to proceed to go-live):
- Model endpoint responds to signed requests from CureTech VPC (latency targets met)
- Persistent KV cache writes survive a single node failover
- All required egress ports allowed and validated in both directions
- Audit logs visible in customer Splunk/Kinesis for the last 24h

Quick answers to your questions:
- Recommended egress: PrivateLink for production (more durable + no public NAT egress). For dev, customer NAT is fine.
- We request a dedicated IAM role for Redwood with least privilege for SSM and limited S3 PutObject (artifact staging).

Action items (owners and deadlines):
- CureTech: confirm whether you want PrivateLink or NAT and share final VPC/subnet IDs (due: Wed 14 Jul) — Nicola / Samir
- Redwood (Laura): draft IAM role policy and DocuSign SOW for Dedicated private deployment (due: Thu 15 Jul) — laura_bennett
- Redwood (Alex): publish the exact port/endpoint CSV and a small test harness that your network team can run (due: Fri 16 Jul) — alex_martinez

Attaching files: redwood-staged-onboard-checklist-v1.xlsx, network-egress-ports.csv

- Karthik
Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Nicola / team — quick technical follow-ups and a short checklist I need from your infra folks to spin up a staging path. Quoting your original details below for context.

On Sat, Jul 10, 2027 at 09:12 Nicola Baines <nicola.baines@curetech.com> wrote:
> AWS account (primary): 111122223333 (us-east-1)
> VPC CIDR: 10.64.0.0/16 (owner-managed)

From the network side please provide:
- Exact subnet IDs for the three zones we'll use (private subnets for workloads and a small public subnet for a NAT/bastion if needed).
- Route table mappings for those subnets and whether you use TGW (Transit Gateway) attachments.
- Whether you allow AWS PrivateLink endpoints to be provisioned in that account (ServiceEndpoint create permission).
- If using TGW/BGP, please provide your ASN and any permitted BGP peers.

Port matrix (minimum required for staging):
- Outbound 443 TCP to redwood-api.private (mTLS)
- Outbound 3500 TCP for control plane heartbeat (we will use mTLS)
- Outbound 53 UDP/TCP for DNS (or configure custom resolver)
- Optional: 22 for bastion jumpbox (restrict to our static office IPs)

Network tuning notes:
- MTU: set to 9001 across host-level path if you plan to run large token batches; otherwise 1500 is ok but you'll see fragmentation.
- Keepalive and idle timeouts: set ELB idle timeout to 120s for streaming sessions.

Smoke harness (what we'll run):
1) Connect to staging endpoint with mutual TLS certificate we provide
2) Run 1-minute p95 latency test for 1KB prompts (target < 70ms additional overhead)
3) Generate 50 concurrent streaming sessions for 2 minutes to validate batching behavior
4) Write/read KV cache; restart one serving node and confirm persistence of writes

If you want we can provide a small EC2-based test runner (push-button script) that your network team runs from inside the target VPC; it performs all the checks above and uploads a JSON report.

I'll attach the simple CSV of ports and an example mTLS cert exchange doc in the Drive link.

- Alex
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
